tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Practical Assessment Technique

questions.question: Q: Describe the structure of a strong NEA portfolio.
questions.correctAnswer: 1) Context and brief. 2) Research: existing products, materials, processes. 3) Specification: measurable criteria. 4) Design development: initial ideas to final design. 5) Manufacturing plan: operations, tools, materials, safety. 6) Manufacture: photographic evidence. 7) Testing and evaluation: compare against specification.

questions.question: Q: Why is annotation important in the NEA portfolio?
questions.correctAnswer: Annotation explains the reasoning behind design decisions. Without annotation, the examiner cannot understand why decisions were made. Good annotation links each decision to a specification requirement or engineering principle.

questions.question: Q: Explain how to evaluate the finished NEA product against the specification.
questions.correctAnswer: Take each specification criterion in turn and test whether the product meets it. Record results with photographic evidence. If any criterion is not met, explain why and suggest improvements.

tests.name: Exam-Style Practice
tests.description: Short-answer practice on Practical Assessment Technique

questions.question: Q: What are the most common mistakes in NEA portfolios?
questions.correctAnswer: 1) Too much irrelevant research. 2) Jumping from brief to final design without showing development. 3) Missing manufacturing plan. 4) Poor annotation. 5) Superficial evaluation.

questions.question: Q: How should you manage your time across the NEA project?
questions.correctAnswer: Allocate roughly: 20% to research and specification, 25% to design development, 15% to planning, 30% to manufacture and 10% to evaluation. Set internal deadlines for each stage.
